key_insight: A dual-resonator planar silver microcavity can both boost sensitizer absorption and improve upconverted light extraction, overcoming a key efficiency bottleneck in solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical photonic design strategy to enhance sub-bandgap photon harvesting in low-intensity photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices without changing the organic chemistry alone.
method: Thermally co-evaporated a rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine (PdPC) active layer inside a planar silver microcavity.
Aligned one dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at 32° to increase sensitizer absorptance.
Used a second cavity mode to directionally out-couple upconverted emission while balancing reabsorption losses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 12-fold increase in absorptance at 665 nm, leading to a 22-fold peak and 4.5-fold integrated enhancement in detected upconversion emission.
watch_item: Cavity benefits may depend strongly on angular alignment and device optical design, and reabsorption losses still need careful management in practical implementations.
paper_title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
